sentences.text: This animal lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
E. T. Newton first described Erpetosuchus in 1894 based on remains found in northeastern Scotland.
The original description included four specimens from the latest Carnian Lossiemouth Sandstone Formation.
American paleontologist Paul E. Olsen discovered a partial skull in 1995 during a field trip in Connecticut, marking the first record found outside Scotland.
This Connecticut specimen was found in the New Haven Formation, which dates to the Norian age.
Erpetosuchus granti was originally assigned to Thecodontia, but this classification is now considered invalid.
An analysis by Olsen et al. in 2000 suggested Erpetosuchus granti is the sister-taxon to Crocodylomorpha.
It is debated whether Erpetosuchus is closely related to Crocodylomorpha, as some analyses suggest an unresolved relationship at the base of Archosauria instead.
